findings.reason: without a control the node can close green on an all-zero answer, which is the defect the section exists to prevent.
findings.text: s24 asserts "Velocity's figures at a revision equal the store's answer over the same runs" and s27 asserts the rebuilt export "answers a capability derivation equal to the pre-untrack answer", but an equality between two arms has no negative control: both arms reading zero, or both reading the same truncated set, satisfies the statement while being exactly the failure s24's own Why names ("would report zero rather than refuse")

findings.reason: a worker sent to create tables that already exist spends its node on a false premise, and the actual gap (no holds writer, append_member unused) goes unnamed.
findings.text: s23 states "members and holds have no tables", but reckon/run_store.py:105-112 defines both `members` and `holds` in _AUX_SCHEMA, and run_store.append_member exists (reckon/run_store.py:871) with no caller anywhere in the tree, so the node as briefed would find the table already present and either report a false blocker or duplicate it; the real work is switching register_member and the reap off ledger.write into the table plus adding the holds writer

findings.reason: s24 cannot be measured where it sits, so it is currently undispatchable or would be closed on half its done-when.
findings.text: s24's done-when requires "a store rebuilt from the export", but the export is delivered by s27, and the declared waits put s27 after s26 after s24, so s24's second arm depends on a capability that lands two nodes later; no export module exists in the tree today (reckon/crew/station_obligations.py:export_snapshot is the only exporter, and it is an obligations snapshot, not the ledger)

findings.reason: the section's measure is unsatisfiable as its stated mechanism, so a node follows it, finds the file persists, and either reports a blocker or weakens its own gate.
findings.text: s21's Why says the repair is to invert _index_append, but append_run writes the per-run file (reckon/ledger.py, target.open("x") at the line before `_bump_generation`) and only then calls `_index_append` (reckon/ledger.py:3521), so a store write that raises leaves the run file behind and the done-when's "leaves no row in either store" is unreachable by inverting the return alone; it needs a store-first order or a compensating unlink, which the section does not state

findings.reason: the scope and the urgency claim are wrong, and the pair with s26 must be resolved one way: either the migration deletes the working-tree copies (making s25's premise true) or it does not (and s25's stated reason needs restating to the fresh-clone case).
findings.text: s25 states that untracking "would silently turn both off in every tree", but both guards key on `(entry / "crew.json").is_file() or (entry / "flight.yaml").is_file()` against the working tree (reckon/hooks/native_agent_guard.py:92, reckon/hooks/worker_message_guard.py:94), and an untracked file still satisfies that test, so in every existing checkout the guards keep firing; the exposure the fix addresses is a fresh tree that never held the ledger

findings.reason: index-only removal contradicts the decision the whole section rests on and leaves the untracked files' fate unnamed, which is the difference between one store and two.
findings.text: s26 declares its write paths as "docs/state/** (removal from the index only)", which leaves docs/state/<project>/crew.json and runs/ present and untracked in every existing checkout, so the run store is not "the only store" the 2026-11-14 decision (line 406) makes it, and two records drift with nothing comparing them
